quiz.title: Quiz 1 - Sequences
quiz.instructions: Work through the questions from foundation to challenge. The first term corresponds to n = 1. Choose one answer, check it, then read the worked solution. Use exact answers.

questions.title: Question 1
questions.prompt: The first four terms of an arithmetic sequence are \(6,\ 10,\ 14,\ 18\). What are the next two terms?

questions.title: Question 2
questions.prompt: An arithmetic sequence begins \(34,\ 28,\ 22,\ 16\). What are the next two terms?
questions.working: Each term decreases by \(6\). The next terms are \(16-6=10\) and \(10-6=4\).

questions.title: Question 3
questions.prompt: Find an expression for the \(n\)th term of the arithmetic sequence \(7,\ 11,\ 15,\ 19,\ldots\).
questions.working: The common difference is \(4\), so the rule is \(4n+c\). The first term gives \(4+c=7\), hence \(c=3\). Therefore the rule is \(4n+3\).

questions.title: Question 4
questions.prompt: An arithmetic sequence starts \(-5,\ 2,\ 9,\ 16,\ldots\). Find its \(n\)th term.
questions.working: The common difference is \(7\). Write \(7n+c\). At \(n=1\), \(7+c=-5\), so \(c=-12\). The rule is \(7n-12\).

questions.title: Question 5
questions.prompt: Find the \(n\)th term of the arithmetic sequence \(11,\ 6,\ 1,\ -4,\ldots\).
questions.working: The difference is \(-5\), so the rule is \(-5n+c\). As \(-5+c=11\), \(c=16\). Thus the rule is \(16-5n\).

questions.title: Question 6
questions.prompt: The \(n\)th term of a sequence is \(3n+8\). Find its 15th term.

questions.title: Question 7
questions.prompt: The \(n\)th term of a sequence is \(9n-4\). Which term has value \(131\)?
questions.working: Solve \(9n-4=131\). Then \(9n=135\) and \(n=15\). It is the 15th term.

questions.title: Question 8
questions.prompt: The \(n\)th term of a sequence is \(4n+1\), where \(n\) is a positive integer. Which number belongs to the sequence?
questions.working: Rearrange \(4n+1=T\) to \(n=\frac{T-1}{4}\). For \(T=93\), \(n=\frac{92}{4}=23\), a positive integer. The other choices give non-integer values of \(n\).

questions.title: Question 9
questions.prompt: The \(n\)th term is \(2n^2-3\). Find the first three terms.

questions.title: Question 10
questions.prompt: A quadratic sequence starts \(5,\ 12,\ 23,\ 38,\ldots\). What is the next term?
questions.working: First differences are \(7,11,15\). The constant second difference is \(4\), so the next first difference is \(19\). The next term is \(38+19=57\).

questions.title: Question 11
questions.prompt: Find the \(n\)th term of the quadratic sequence \(2,\ 5,\ 10,\ 17,\ 26,\ldots\).
questions.working: The first differences are \(3,5,7,9\), so the second difference is \(2\). The coefficient of \(n^2\) is \(1\). Subtract \(1,4,9,16,25\) from the sequence: the remainder is always \(1\). Hence the rule is \(n^2+1\).

questions.title: Question 12
questions.prompt: A quadratic sequence begins \(4,\ 13,\ 28,\ 49,\ 76,\ldots\). Find its \(n\)th term.
questions.working: The first differences are \(9,15,21,27\); second differences are \(6\). Therefore the coefficient of \(n^2\) is \(3\). Subtract \(3n^2\) from the corresponding terms: \(4-3=1\), \(13-12=1\), \(28-27=1\). The rule is \(3n^2+1\).

questions.title: Question 13
questions.prompt: Find the \(n\)th term of the quadratic sequence \(-2,\ 3,\ 12,\ 25,\ldots\).
questions.working: First differences are \(5,9,13\) and second differences are \(4\), so start with \(2n^2\). Subtract \(2n^2\) from the sequence to get \(-4,-5,-6,-7\), whose rule is \(-n-3\). Add this to obtain \(2n^2-n-3\).

questions.title: Question 14
questions.prompt: The 4th term of an arithmetic sequence is \(17\) and its 10th term is \(47\). Find the \(n\)th term.
questions.working: There are \(10-4=6\) equal steps between the terms. Thus the difference is \(d=\frac{47-17}{6}=5\). The rule is \(5n+c\). Using the 4th term, \(20+c=17\), so \(c=-3\). Hence the rule is \(5n-3\).

questions.title: Question 15
questions.prompt: The \(n\)th term of a sequence is \(n^2+3n-2\), for positive integers \(n\). Which term has value \(106\)?
questions.working: Set \(n^2+3n-2=106\), so \(n^2+3n-108=0\). Factorise: \((n+12)(n-9)=0\). The roots are \(-12\) and \(9\). Term positions must be positive integers, so it is the 9th term. Check: \(9^2+3(9)-2=106\).
